when: Week 1, days 3–7, evening sessions. About 12 hours.

sittings.bodyEn: Project 2 proves you understand the Transformer and can write PyTorch, not only call an API. You build and train a small character-level GPT on Indonesian text while typing along with Karpathy’s video. When someone asks for 大模型原理, this is the artifact you open. Honest limit: a pasted notebook you cannot explain line by line is worse than no project.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean how a large model works under the hood.

sittings.bodyEn: Watch Andrej Karpathy’s “Let’s build GPT” while typing in a notebook — do not paste his finished file. Typing yourself makes tensor shapes stick when you explain later. Download a few million characters of Indonesian Wikipedia into a text file for training. Honest limit: watching without typing feels fast and leaves you empty in a live code review.

Read the model top to bottom: attention head, multi-head, block with residual and LayerNorm, then embeddings and the final linear. Point at the causal mask and be ready to say what happens without it. Run a short smoke test and check whether first loss is near ln of the vocab size. Honest limit: if you cannot point at the mask, keep reading before the long train.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean block attention from looking at future tokens.

sittings.bodyEn: Run the full train and copy loss into a table for train and validation at fixed steps. If validation rises while training falls, say you are overfitting — that is a good finding. Change one thing at a time: fewer layers, shorter block size, then temperature. Honest limit: three knobs changed together give you no experiment story.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean train loss falls while validation loss rises.

sittings.bodyEn: Done means a roughly million-parameter GPT you can explain line by line, including the causal mask. You have a loss table, three honest experiments, and sample text from the model. The README states real differences from Qwen: characters not subwords, learned positions not RoPE, few blocks, no instruction tuning. Honest limit: claiming “like Qwen” without those differences will get challenged.

Without the causal mask, loss can fall near zero without learning language, because the model peeks ahead. First loss should be about ln V because probability starts evenly spread. Your smoke-test numbers will not match any book exactly — report yours. Never put unfinished training on the CV as done. Honest limit: inventing a matching loss is worse than an ugly real table.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean tokens attend to other tokens in the sequence.

sittings.titleEn: Why first loss is ln V
sittings.bodyEn: At the start the model spreads probability evenly over the vocabulary. Cross-entropy for that uniform guess is about ln of the vocab size.
sittings.prompt: Why should the first training loss be about ln of the vocabulary size?
choices: Because the optimizer starts at learning rate ln(V)
Because at the start the model spreads probability evenly over V characters
Because causal masking multiplies loss by ln(V)
Because LayerNorm forces loss to ln(V)

sittings.bodyEn: The causal mask stops attention from looking ahead. Without it, loss can collapse without learning language.
sittings.prompt: What does the causal mask prevent, and what happens without it?
choices: It prevents overfitting; without it validation loss always rises
It prevents looking at future characters; without it loss can fall near zero without learning
It prevents using more than four layers
